title: Pitch playbook: compact economics & risk scripts
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook gives field teams a compact, repeatable set of messaging scripts, competitive talking points, pricing heuristics, and a short customer case study to accelerate technical discovery conversations with platform and engineering buyers. It is optimized for 10–25 minute technical deep dives and CISO/Finance readiness checks.

Who this is for
- Sales Engineers: concise scripts for demos and risk conversations.
- Account Executives: framing snippets for exec/C-level briefs.
- Solution Architects: competitive countermeasures and deployment notes.

Positioning pillars (30-second soundbites)
1) Predictable inference economics: "Redwood converts model choices into predictable per-token costs via quantization profiles, smart batching, and autoscaling policies—so you can forecast ML spend like any other infra line item."
2) Production-grade reliability: "We provide SLAs, fallbacks, and dedicated capacity options so user-facing LLM features stay online even under load or model regressions."
3) Deployment flexibility and security: "Host with Redwood, or deploy Redwood Private into your VPC / on-prem—with KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs for regulated workloads."
4) Developer-first operations: "Same API, tooling, and rollouts across hosted, dedicated, and private—reduces cognitive load for platform teams."

Competitive brief (quick reference)
- OpenAI / Anthropic (hosted LLM APIs)
  - Strengths: largest model ecosystem, simple API, fast time-to-prototype.
  - Redwood response: Emphasize SLO-backed dedicated capacity, cost controls (batching/quant), and enterprise security for regulated customers. Highlight predictable unit economics and rollout controls.
- Cloud-managed endpoints (AWS SageMaker, GCP Vertex)
  - Strengths: deep cloud integration, billing consolidation.
  - Redwood response: Stress inference-optimized runtime (KV cache, continuous batching) that typically reduces per-token runtime by 20–40% vs generic endpoint configurations; point to dedicated GPU pool options and multi-cloud routing.
- Self-hosted runtime vendors (open-source runtimes/orchestration)
  - Strengths: control, no vendor lock.
  - Redwood response: Call out the operational burden, ongoing kernel selection, and performance tuning required. Position Redwood as a managed alternative that preserves control (Private deployment) while removing engineering debt.

Quick battlecards (friction points + counters)
- "We can just run this ourselves on EC2/GKE."
  - Counter: For sustained user-facing latency SLOs, the engineering cost of kernel tuning, KV cache correctness, and autoscaling policy development is non-trivial. Offer a 6–8 week pilot that shows unit-cost delta and time-to-market delta.
- "OpenAI has better models / quality."
  - Counter: Redwood supports model rollouts and automatic fallback to tuned variants; for many production workloads model parity is not the primary constraint—latency, cost, and observability are. Offer a side-by-side eval with traffic replay.

Demo scripts: 12-minute technical deep dive (structure)
1) 0:00–1:30 — 30-second product framing & value props (use positioning pillars).
2) 1:30–4:00 — Live trace: show Console call graph, per-token cost breakdown, and latency SLOs for a sample chat workload.
3) 4:00–7:00 — Deployment options: toggle to Dedicated and simulated failover to Private mock (show routing policy UI + audit logs).
4) 7:00–10:00 — Economics toggle: show autoscaling, batching, and quantization profiles and an on-screen estimator for per-10k tokens cost.
5) 10:00–12:00 — Security & compliance quick tour: KMS key rotation demo, RBAC role preview, and a link to compliance evidence pack.

Concise SE scripts (one-liners and short paragraphs)
- For platform engineers: "You can pin model versions and route traffic by latency or cost tiers so your product teams get consistent latency while finance keeps predictable billing."
- For CISO/InfoSec: "We integrate with customer KMS and provide immutable audit logs per request; Private installs run entirely in your VPC and optionally air-gapped environments."
- For Finance: "Our optimizer provides cost-sensitivity controls—scale down quantization for low-risk workloads and reserve Dedicated capacity for high-throughput endpoints to cap spend."

Pricing guidance (heuristic framework)
- Pricing levers to discuss: model class, dedicated capacity vs hosted, latency SLO, caching hit rate, and quantization profile.
- Sample scenarios (illustrative; use the pricing calculator for final quotes):

| Scenario | Model class | Traffic pattern | Key levers | Expected per-10k token cost (est) |
|---|---:|---|---|---:|
| Small chatbot MVP | Llama2-13B quantized | 10 reqs/s bursts | aggressive batching, prefix caching | $1.20 |
| Customer support scale | Llama2-70B trimmed | 50 reqs/s sustained | Dedicated pool, conservative quant | $5.60 |
| Document embeddings | Efficient embed model | batch offline | batch-only, high throughput | $0.08 |

- Pricing talking tips: always include three levers customers can act on immediately (batching, cache, quantization) and show dollarized impact in the demo. Use committed Dedicated capacity to cap unit costs for high-throughput endpoints.

Security FAQ for prospects (top 8 questions)
1) Where are request logs stored and who can access them?
   - Answer: Request logs are stored in the customer’s control plane for Private deployments or in a tenant-isolated storage layer for Hosted; access is RBAC-controlled and recorded in audit logs.
2) How do you handle encryption and key management?
   - Answer: We support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM; keys are never exported to third parties in Private deployments.
3) Can we run Redwood in a fully air-gapped environment?
   - Answer: Yes — an on-prem package is available with an install guide and cross-checklist.
4) How do you support data residency and retention policies?
   - Answer: Per-route retention settings and legal hold controls are available; we provide exportable evidence for audits.
5) What is your incident notification and SLA for security incidents?
   - Answer: We follow our security incident playbook; affected customers receive email + console notifications within 2 hours and a root-cause summary within 72 hours for P1 security incidents.
6) How are model weights/vulnerable artifacts controlled in Private installs?
   - Answer: Model artifacts are stored in customer-managed artifact stores with provenance metadata; automated checks prevent execution of unsigned artifacts.
7) Do you provide penetration test reports and SOC/compliance evidence?
   - Answer: Yes — we supply SOC2 Type II reports and pen test summaries in the compliance evidence pack; for dedicated/Private customers we provide redacted reports as appropriate.
8) How do you prevent model extraction or prompt-injection leakage?
   - Answer: We recommend a layered approach: response filtering, graduation of quantization for sensitive models, request size and rate limits, and application-layer input validation; we also provide monitoring that detects anomalous query patterns.

Short customer case study (anonymized)
- Customer: "FinScale" (financial SaaS platform, mid-market)
- Problem: Unpredictable inference costs and frequent user-visible latency spikes as demand scaled from 5k to 50k daily queries.
- Solution: Migrated 3 high-volume customer-facing endpoints to Redwood Dedicated, applied prefix caching and conservative quantization profile, and set autoscaling policies with burst capacity.
- Outcome (90 days):
  - 38% reduction in per-token runtime latency (median p50)-> from 230ms to 143ms.
  - 27% reduction in unit inference spend vs their prior cloud endpoint configuration.
  - Zero production incidents during Black Friday-like traffic test.

Objection handling cheat sheet
- "We need to keep everything in-house for compliance." => Offer Private deployment checklist and propose a technical pilot in their lab environment with our SRE support.
- "This is a pricing/ROI conversation." => Use the per-10k demo estimator and propose a 30-day traffic replay pilot to measure delta.
- "Model quality concerns." => Offer traffic-split rollouts and A/B evaluation harness; commit to quality regression alerts tied to their prompt set.

Next steps & pilot template (3-step rapid pilot)
1) Align scope (week 0): Confirm 2 endpoints, traffic replay dataset, and success metrics (latency p50/p95, cost per 10k tokens).
2) Pilot (weeks 1–3): Deploy Redwood in org trial mode or light Private deployment, run traffic replay, and tune batching/cache/quant profiles. Provide daily checkpoint notes.
3) Wrap & decision (week 4): Deliver ROI report, long-term capacity recommendation, and a production rollout checklist.
